Quick update from runtime/ops:
- We observed an increased request fanout to the eastmed-AZ that correlated with a regional network fabric degradation at ~08:49 UTC. Packet retries at the host level increased; NVLink errors on a subset of nodes caused the serving scheduler to concentrate traffic (less even distribution) which amplified queuing latency.
- KV cache hit rates dropped ~18% for NovaHealth prefixes between 08:50-09:10 which explains higher compute per request and longer tails.
- We rolled a temporary routing policy at 10:05 UTC (auto-led policy) to shift 40% of traffic off eastmed to eu-west-1 for affected prefixes; errors decreased to ~0.9% and p99 dropped to ~720ms.

Actions taken:
1) Temporary traffic steering to eu-west-1 (10:05) — partial relief.
2) Evacuated 6/18 nodes in eastmed-AZ that reported NVLink errors; manual drain continues.
3) Increasing batch timeout thresholds to avoid mid-request timeouts for affected requests.

Remaining asks:
- Confirm customer can tolerate 40% cross-region steer (possible cost/latency tradeoff). Rafael, can you get explicit OK from NovaHealth?
- Ben, please continue KV cache warm-up scripts and track re-hit rate.

Sooj

- If you prefer not to cross-region steer, we can instead spin reserved capacity in eastmed (estimated 12-18m to provision) and reroute traffic back once fully healthy.
